title: Certificates of Deposit: Published Rates, the Jumbo Bonus and How a Term's Rate Is Set
content:
Every term of one of the bank's Certificates of Deposit earns one interest rate and shows one APY, and both are locked in when the term begins. This page gives Piedmont Crescent Bank's published standard figures for each tier, the Jumbo Bonus, and the way bonus points combine with the standard figures.

## How the rate of a term is set

The rate of a term is fixed on the day the term starts and does not move with later changes to the published figures. It equals the tier's published standard interest rate plus any bonus points the term has earned. Those very bonus points, added to the tier's published standard APY, give the term's APY.

Two bonuses exist and no others: the Jumbo Bonus and the Relationship Bonus. When both are earned they are simply added together, and the combined points are added once to the standard rate and once to the standard APY.

## The Jumbo Bonus

The Jumbo Bonus adds the tier's Jumbo Bonus points to both the rate and the APY when two things are true: the tier offers the Jumbo Bonus, and the certificate's principal at the start of the term is at least the tier's Jumbo Bonus threshold. For a newly opened certificate, that principal is the opening deposit.

For a renewed term, the earlier basis under which the principal tested was the recorded balance on the renewal date following any add-ons and withdrawals made during grace is **no longer in force**; the principal on which a renewal's Jumbo Bonus is tested is now governed by the current renewal basis.

## Published figures by tier

| Tier | Standard APY (%) | Standard interest rate (%) | Jumbo Bonus offered | Jumbo Bonus threshold | Jumbo Bonus points |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6-Month Certificate | 3.85 | 3.78 | Yes | USD 100000.00 | 0.10 |
| 11-Month No-Penalty Certificate | 3.60 | 3.54 | No | USD 100000.00 | 0.00 |
| 12-Month Certificate | 4.05 | 3.97 | Yes | USD 100000.00 | 0.10 |
| 18-Month Bump-Up Certificate | 3.90 | 3.83 | Yes | USD 100000.00 | 0.10 |
| 36-Month Certificate | 3.55 | 3.49 | Yes | USD 100000.00 | 0.10 |
| 60-Month Certificate | 3.45 | 3.39 | Yes | USD 100000.00 | 0.10 |

The standard APY is the yield produced by compounding the standard interest rate daily; both are the figures currently published for a new term, before any bonus.

## Worked examples (hypothetical openings)

- A 12-Month Certificate opened with USD 150000.00 and no Relationship Bonus: the Jumbo Bonus applies, so the term's rate is 3.97 plus 0.10, that is 4.07 percent, and its APY is 4.05 plus 0.10, that is 4.15 percent.
- The same certificate opened with USD 99999.99: below the threshold, no Jumbo Bonus; rate 3.97 percent, APY 4.05 percent.
- Exactly USD 100000.00 into a 36-Month Certificate: the threshold is met, so the Jumbo Bonus applies.
- USD 400000.00 into an 11-Month No-Penalty Certificate: the tier does not offer the Jumbo Bonus, so no Jumbo points are added whatever the size.

## Points of judgement

**Can a later deposit add the Jumbo Bonus to a running term?** No. The rate is fixed when the term starts; the principal tested is the principal at that start.
